question: Which of the following units is used to measure the intensity of sound?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Decibel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The intensity of sound is measured in units called **decibels (dB)**.
 
• Decibels are a logarithmic unit used to express the **ratio of two values of a physical quantity**, often power or intensity.
 
• A sound level of 0 dB is considered the threshold of hearing, while 120-130 dB is the threshold of pain.
 
• Every 10 dB increase represents a tenfold increase in intensity, meaning a sound at 30 dB is ten times more intense than a sound at 20 dB.
 
• The decibel scale is used in various fields including **acoustics, electronics, and control theory**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pascal (Pa)**

 
 
• Pascal is the SI unit of **pressure**.
 
• It is defined as one **newton per square meter**.
 
 
 
• **Joule (J)**
 
 
• Joule is the SI unit of **energy**.
 
• It is defined as the energy transferred when one newton of force moves an object one meter.
 
 
 
• **Curie (Ci)**
 
 
• Curie is a unit of **radioactivity**.
 
• It is defined as **3.7 × 10^10 decays per second**.
